graph.summary: Gabapentin → Voltage-dependent calcium channel subunit alpha-2/delta-1 → calcium ion transmembrane transport → neurotransmitter secretion → Epilepsy

evidence.snippet: α2δ proteins are the targets of the widely prescribed anti-epileptic and anti-allodynic drugs gabapentin and pregabalin
evidence.explanation: Gabapentin binds to the α2δ-1 (CACNA2D1) auxiliary subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, acting as a high-affinity ligand that reduces its functional activity.

paper.title: Neuronal α2δ proteins and brain disorders.
paper.journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology

evidence.snippet: The α 2 δ-1 protein is required for the ability of gabapentin and pregabalin to reduce neurotransmitter release in neuronal tissue, consistent with a therapeutic mechanism of action via voltage-gated calcium channels.
evidence.explanation: The α2δ-1 protein is both the high-affinity binding site and required mediator of gabapentin's mechanism, confirming gabapentin decreases its activity.

paper.title: Analgesia with Gabapentin and Pregabalin May Involve N-Methyl-d-Aspartate Receptors, Neurexins, and Thrombospondins.
paper.journal: The Journal of pharmacology and experimental therapeutics

evidence.snippet: All alpha2delta subunits increase the density at the plasma membrane of Ca(2+) channels activated by high voltage
evidence.explanation: The α2δ-1 subunit promotes trafficking of voltage-gated calcium channels to the plasma membrane, thereby positively regulating calcium ion transmembrane transport.

paper.title: Functional biology of the alpha(2)delta subunits of voltage-gated calcium channels.

evidence.snippet: They serve as regulatory subunits of voltage-gated calcium channels
evidence.explanation: As a regulatory subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels, α2δ-1 positively regulates calcium ion flux across the neuronal membrane.

paper.title: Neuronal α2δ proteins and brain disorders.
paper.journal: Pflugers Archiv : European journal of physiology

evidence.snippet: They inhibit calcium mediated neurotransmitter release through effects on α2δ-1 subunits
evidence.explanation: Calcium-mediated neurotransmitter release is explicitly invoked — calcium ion transmembrane transport drives (positively regulates) neurotransmitter secretion at presynaptic terminals.

paper.title: Analgesic mechanisms of gabapentinoids and effects in experimental pain models: a narrative review.

evidence.snippet: GBPs reduced release of various neurotransmitters from synapses in several neuronal tissues
evidence.explanation: Gabapentinoids reduce neurotransmitter release by modulating presynaptic Ca2+ currents, consistent with calcium influx positively driving neurotransmitter secretion.

paper.title: Acute modulation of calcium currents and synaptic transmission by gabapentinoids.

evidence.snippet: Pregabalin subtly reduces the synaptic release of several neurotransmitters, apparently by binding to alpha2-delta subunits, and possibly accounting for its actions in vivo to reduce neuronal excitability and seizures
evidence.explanation: Reducing neurotransmitter secretion reduces neuronal excitability and seizures; conversely, excess neurotransmitter secretion contributes to the seizure activity that defines epilepsy.

paper.title: Pharmacology and mechanism of action of pregabalin: the calcium channel alpha2-delta (alpha2-delta) subunit as a target for antiepileptic drug discovery.

evidence.snippet: reduction of abnormal neuronal excitability through reduced neurotransmitter release
evidence.explanation: Abnormal neurotransmitter release drives neuronal hyperexcitability and epileptic seizures; reducing secretion is the therapeutic rationale, confirming secretion contributes to epilepsy.

paper.title: Pharmacology and mechanism of action of pregabalin: the calcium channel alpha2-delta (alpha2-delta) subunit as a target for antiepileptic drug discovery.
